## Welcome

This deck is the shared sample used to preview **every** theme in this
collection. It exercises the elements most talks need:

- Plain bullet points, with [links](https://quarto.org/docs/presentations/revealjs/)
  and `inline code`
- [Alerts]{.alert} and [highlighted phrases]{.highlight}
    - and nested bullets
- Code, tables, callouts, quotes and columns

# Writing

## Text and emphasis

Slides should say one thing well. Use **bold** for weight, *italics* for tone
and [alert]{.alert} for the one phrase the audience must remember.

> Code runs where the prose lives, so results never drift out of date.

Numbered lists work too:

1. Write your analysis in plain text
2. Render to slides, documents or websites
3. Re-render whenever the data changes

## Two columns

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}
### Left

- One source document
- Many output formats
- Version control friendly
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
### Right

- HTML slides via reveal.js
- PDF via Typst or LaTeX
- Word, PowerPoint and more

# Computation

## Code runs where the prose lives

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="45%"}
- Chunks execute at render time
- Results stay in sync with the text
- Skip re-runs with `freeze: auto`
- See the [reveal.js guide](https://quarto.org/docs/presentations/revealjs/)
:::

::: {.column width="55%"}
```python
# mean bill length by species
import seaborn as sns

df = sns.load_dataset("penguins")
(df.groupby("species")
   .bill_length_mm
   .mean()
   .round(1))
```
:::

::::

## Maths and callouts

The mean of $n$ observations is

$$
\bar{x} = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^{n} x_i
$$

::: {.callout-note}
Callouts come in five flavours: note, tip, important, caution and warning.
:::
